html:
SMTO-LLM-0079 — The model server action was cancelled

GUID: 6a7177b8-c53d-54a8-b830-c910ffd33cde
Slug: local-ai-operation-cancelled
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • The model server action was stopped before it finished. Depending on when it stopped, nothing may have changed, or a model server may have started and been stopped, or part of a model may have downloaded.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In a new message, ask SMTO to list the model servers and installed models on that Gateway. This shows whether the cancelled action left a running server or a partial download behind.
  2. If a model server from the cancelled start still shows as running or unknown, ask the person who manages the Gateway computer to check it before starting another. A leftover server would clash with a new one over the same port and graphics card.
  3. When you know what's there, ask SMTO to do the action again if you still want it. Once the leftover state is clear, repeating the request won't duplicate work.

What success looks like

  • The list of model servers and installed models on that Gateway matches what you expect.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway computer. Don't start the same model server twice while an earlier one might still be running.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Local AI operation was cancelled before dispatch, during admission, during an Ollama pull or after a runtime was spawned; the receipt's executed/effect_unknown fields show which, and partial downloads or runtimes may exist.

What this means

  • Cancellation can precede dispatch, interrupt a model pull or stop an already spawned runtime; executed and unknown-effect facts distinguish those cases. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • Cancellation can precede dispatch, interrupt a model pull or stop an already spawned runtime; executed and unknown-effect facts distinguish those cases.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the cancellation receipt, runtime ID and model inventory; do not infer no effects from the word cancelled.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the receipt's executed and effect_unknown fields, then run local_ai.runtimes and local_ai.models on the profile's Gateway to account for any spawned runtime or partial pull. Request a new operation (with a new execution ID) only after that state is known.
  • Reconcile the recorded operation and partial state before asking for a replacement action.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • The original operation has a conclusive receipt and any partial runtime/download state is accounted for.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
